peperomia-ferreyrae: 'Happy Bean' peperomia has leaves like little green beans — each one a water tank for dry weather.
echinopsis-cucumber-cactus: Echinopsis cacti produce some of the largest flowers in the cactus family — huge blooms from a spiky little body.
crasula-ovata: In feng shui the jade plant is a money magnet — its round leaves resemble coins, hence 'money tree'.
echiveria-sempervivum: Its Latin name means 'always alive' — Sempervivum shrugs off frost and drought that kill most plants.
eed-tip-sempervivum: Sempervivum is called 'hens and chicks' — the mother rosette raises baby rosettes around herself all season.
golden-cypress: Golden cypress keeps its chartreuse colour year-round — a rare evergreen that stays bright in winter too.
madhukamini-dwarf: Madhukamini (orange jasmine) perfumes the evening air — its fragrance carries farthest after dusk.
dracena-white-victoria: Dracaena cultivars are named like royalty for a reason — this one's white-striped leaves glow in low light.
snake-plant-senseveria: Snake plants were part of NASA's famous clean-air study — filtering formaldehyde and benzene from indoor air.
croton-codiaeum-variegatum: A croton's reds and yellows come from pigments that intensify with light — more sun, more colour.
geranium: Geraniums were carried on ocean voyages — Victorian sailors grew them in ship portholes for a taste of home.
ixora-dwarf-2: Ixora's flower clusters open a few blooms at a time, so one plant stays in colour for months, not weeks.
yellow-dwarf-tecoma: Tecoma flowers continuously in warm weather — a single shrub can bloom nearly all year in Indore's climate.
mitha-neem: Mitha neem ('sweet neem') isn't a neem at all — it's Chinaberry, a different tree entirely that just resembles one.
belpatra: Belpatra's trifoliate leaves — three leaflets on one stalk — are why it's offered to Lord Shiva in temples.
